actionable_lessons: As I look back on their influence on me—and on the ideas in this book— I see that these women instinctively knew what we all need to understand, appreciate, and master today.
arguments: They each had exquisite taste, and the success of their businesses was built on that.

During the same era, my maternal grandmother, Omi, brought her flair for design and dressmaking to the gentry of South Africa, where she made and marketed evening gowns inspired by the grand couturiers of Paris.
Their businesses may have survived because of hard work and discipline, but they thrived because of their founders’ aesthetic intelligence.
examples: Then there is her world-class team at HarperCollins—the brilliant marketing and publicity trio Brian Perrin, Penny Makras, and Rachel Elinsky; production editor, Nikki Baldauf; production supervisor, Jocelyn Larnick; and book designer, William Ruoto.

stories: Acknowledgments I come from a long line of powerful women.
Both my grandmothers founded and ran their own businesses.

My paternal grandmother, Granny Hedy, owned a line of high-end children’s clothing, which she launched in the 1940s at her Long Island, New York, kitchen table and eventually sold to boutiques across the United States.
